key_insight: Inherent decoding randomness limits how accurately LLM output length can be predicted from prefill hidden states, with tested predictors approaching this limit.
engineering_relevance: Inference schedulers should account for irreducible length uncertainty rather than expect predictor upgrades alone to eliminate scheduling error.
method: Model autoregressive decoding as a stopped stochastic process with a gradually increasing stopping probability.
Derive per-prompt approximate normality, prediction-error bounds, and the affine standard-deviation law σ = αμ + b.
Compare MLP, EGTP, FiLM, soft-label, and Mixture-of-Experts predictors under fixed evaluation conditions.
evidence_signal: The normal approximation reproduces per-prompt MAE and central distribution mass within a few percent, while diverse predictors achieve similar performance near the derived bound.
watch_item: Benchmark comparisons must fix the target model, dataset, and sampling parameters; report relative as well as absolute errors to avoid conflating predictor quality with task difficulty.
paper_title: On the Fundamental Limits of Prefill-Based Decoding Length Prediction
